en.p: In coordinate space there is a sphere with center $\mathrm{C}(2,\,\sqrt{5},\,5)$ passing through the point $\mathrm{P}(0,\,0,\,1)$:

For a point Q moving on the circle formed where sphere $S$ meets the plane OPC and a point R moving on sphere $S$, let $\mathrm{Q_1}$, $\mathrm{R_1}$ be the orthogonal projections of the two points Q, R onto the $xy$-plane, respectively.

For the two points Q, R that maximize the area of triangle $\mathrm{OQ_1R_1}$, the area of the orthogonal projection of triangle $\mathrm{OQ_1R_1}$ onto the plane PQR is $\dfrac{q}{p}\sqrt{6}$. Find the value of $p+q$. (Here O is the origin, the three points O, $\mathrm{Q_1}$, $\mathrm{R_1}$ are not collinear, and $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime natural numbers.) [4 points]
